title: Design a Payment System (idempotency, ledger, reconciliation)
relevance: High — correctness-heavy HLD at Stripe / OpenAI / fintech + FAANG / Indian product cos (PhonePe, Razorpay, Flipkart Pay, Uber); probes idempotency, double-entry ledger, and reconciliation more than raw QPS.
company_notes: Very common full round for experienced/fintech/Stripe-adjacent tracks with depth on idempotency, ledger, recon, and PCI; less common than URL shortener/chat for campus/new-grad but rising at product cos with payments (PhonePe, Razorpay, Amazon, Uber, Flipkart), often as checkout or UPI; high frequency on backend/fintech tracks — treat the three pillars (idempotency, ledger, reconciliation) as mandatory if targeting payments companies.

phases.goal: Lock e-commerce pay-in scope via a third-party PSP, core charge/status/idempotency FRs, and correctness-first NFRs (integrity, durability, PCI).

must_hit.point: Clarify product as Amazon-style e-commerce pay-in charging a card via a third-party PSP (Stripe/Braintree); not building VisaNet or a consumer wallet app — say scope out loud.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks one product (usually e-commerce + PSP) and explicitly rules out card-network or full wallet-app scope.

must_hit.point: Core FRs: create/charge a payment; track status (pending / succeeded / failed); survive retries without double charge.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names charge + status tracking + no-double-charge under retry before drawing boxes.

must_hit.point: NFRs: financial integrity (no double charge / lost settle); durability + auditability; PCI so raw cards never hit your servers; CP for money mutations; interview scale often ~1k–10k TPS peak (Hello Interview ~10k).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Leads with correctness/audit/PCI and strong consistency on money writes rather than flashy QPS math.

must_hit.point: Optional FRs if asked: partial/full refunds, merchant payouts, saved payment methods, multi-seller cart; out of scope unless probed: building card networks, full fraud ML, multi-currency FX engine, chargeback workflows.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates must-haves from optional and names what stays below the line.

probes: What product are we building, and what must never go wrong on the payment path?

hints.1: Start by naming the product and the money-safety properties before components.
hints.2: Separate create/charge + status tracking from optional refunds/payouts, and call out PCI/no raw PAN.
hints.3: Say e-commerce pay-in via PSP; FRs charge + pending/succeeded/failed + no double charge on retry; NFRs integrity, durability/audit, PCI, CP on money writes, ~1k–10k TPS peak.

phases.goal: Show you can size QPS/storage while treating correctness as primary; latency dominated by PSP, not your DB.

must_hit.point: Example: 10M payments / day ≈ 115 TPS avg; peak 5–10× → design for ~1k TPS (or use interviewer’s 10k).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States assumptions aloud and converts daily volume to avg/peak TPS without pretending throughput is the main risk.

must_hit.point: Payload ~1 KB/payment plus 2–4 ledger lines → tens of GB/day raw; retain years → partition/archive ledger by time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sizes payment + ledger write volume and concludes time-based partition/archive.

must_hit.point: Sync path latency budget dominated by PSP RTT (100s of ms), not your DB; one SQL primary can start; shard by merchant_id / payment_id when hot merchants or write volume demand it — don’t invent Kafka for the charge itself.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Blames PSP RTT for latency and keeps the charge path on SQL until sharding is justified.

probes: Walk through back-of-envelope for payments/day → TPS and why storage/latency matter differently than a chat system.

hints.1: Pick a daily payment count and convert to average and peak TPS.
hints.2: Add per-payment bytes and ledger lines, then say what dominates sync latency.
hints.3: Use 10M/day ≈ 115 TPS avg, peak 5–10× → ~1k TPS (or 10k); ~1 KB + 2–4 ledger lines; PSP RTT in the 100s of ms; SQL first, shard by merchant_id/payment_id later.

phases.goal: Define idempotent payment/refund APIs, PSP webhook intake, and token-only card handling.

must_hit.point: POST /v1/payments with header Idempotency-Key: <uuid> and body { amount, currency, merchant_id, customer_id, payment_method_token, capture_method? } → { payment_id, status, client_secret? }.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows create-payment with Idempotency-Key and tokenized payment method, not raw card fields.

must_hit.point: GET /v1/payments/{payment_id} for status + amounts; POST /v1/payments/{payment_id}/refunds with its own idempotency key; POST /v1/webhooks/psp for inbound PSP events with signature verification.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers read, refunds (idempotent), and verified inbound PSP webhooks.

must_hit.point: Never accept raw card PAN on your API when designing a merchant platform — accept tokens from Elements / PSP.js.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects PAN in the request body and points to hosted fields/tokenization.

probes: What does create-payment look like, and how do retries and PSP callbacks show up in the API?

hints.1: Start from the client call that creates a charge.
hints.2: Add Idempotency-Key, refunds, and a verified PSP webhook endpoint.
hints.3: POST /v1/payments with Idempotency-Key + token body; GET status; POST refunds with its own key; POST /v1/webhooks/psp with signature verify; no raw PAN.

phases.goal: Model payment state machine, durable idempotency, append-only double-entry ledger, wallet, outbox, and reconciliation runs.

must_hit.point: payments(payment_id PK, merchant_id, customer_id, amount, currency, status state machine, psp_reference, idempotency_key UNIQUE per merchant scope, created_at, updated_at).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Has a payments row with status + PSP reference + scoped unique idempotency key.

must_hit.point: idempotency_records(scope, key UNIQUE, request_hash, response_body, status_code, created_at with TTL ~24h Stripe-style or longer); ledger_accounts + append-only ledger_entries grouped by journal_id that must sum to zero.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates key→cached response store from double-entry journal lines that balance.

must_hit.point: wallets(merchant_id, currency, available_balance, held_balance, version); outbox(...); reconciliation_runs(...); enforce UNIQUE(idempotency_key) and balanced journal in the same DB transaction as status transitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties wallet/outbox/recon tables to transactional invariants on status changes.

probes: What tables do you need so retries cannot double-charge and every money move leaves an audit trail?

hints.1: Think payment row, idempotency cache, and ledger — not just a balance column.
hints.2: Add journal lines that balance, wallet version, outbox, and recon runs.
hints.3: payments with scoped unique idempotency_key + status; idempotency_records (~24h TTL); ledger_entries under journal_id summing to 0; wallets + outbox + reconciliation_runs enforced in the same TX.

phases.goal: Wire checkout → payment service/executor → PSP → wallet/ledger, with outbox webhooks and nightly settlement reconciliation.

must_hit.point: Alex Xu shape: Payment service (orchestrate) → Payment executor (call PSP) → PSP/card schemes → Wallet (merchant balance) → Ledger (immutable journal); checkout uses Stripe.js/Elements so PAN never hits your servers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws the five-stage money path and tokens card data at the edge.

must_hit.point: Flow: check idempotency key → return cached if hit; else insert payment (pending) + outbox in same TX; executor HTTPS to PSP; on success (sync or webhook) Wallet update + Ledger journal in an ACID TX; outbox relay → queue → merchant webhooks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sequences idempotency → pending+outbox TX → PSP → wallet/ledger TX → async merchant notify.

must_hit.point: Nightly: PSP settlement file → Reconciliation job ↔ Ledger → alert/repair queue; SQL (Postgres) is source of truth for payments+ledger; Redis optional only as cache in front of durable idempotency store; transactional outbox (or CDC) avoids dual-write loss.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds settlement reconciliation and names DB as SoT with outbox for publish atomicity.

probes: Walk the path from Buy click to ledger write and merchant webhook — where is the source of truth?

hints.2: Put idempotency and outbox on the write path, webhooks/settlement on the async path.
hints.3: Payment service → executor → PSP; pending+outbox same TX; wallet+ledger ACID; outbox→queue→webhooks; nightly settlement file reconciled to ledger; Postgres SoT.

phases.goal: Defend idempotency, double-entry ledger, sync+webhook confirmation, reconciliation adjustments, and saga/outbox for multi-step money flows.

must_hit.point: Idempotency: persist in-progress under the client key before calling PSP, also send a PSP-side idempotency key, then finalize; same client key must never create two PSP charges; compare params on replay (Stripe rejects mismatched body).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Stores key state before the PSP call and explains replay returns the first result without a second charge.

must_hit.point: Ledger vs mutable balance only: double-entry append-only journal (≥2 lines summing to zero) is the interview answer for audit/recon; cached wallets.balance updated in the same TX as ledger lines (or derived asynchronously with care).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects balance-only as primary books and describes balancing debit/credit lines plus optional cached balance.

must_hit.point: Sync PSP call vs async webhook: design for both — optimistic pending + durable webhook handler idempotent on psp_event_id; webhooks/polling are source of truth for delayed/3DS, not only the sync HTTP response.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Does not trust sync alone; webhook handler dedupes on event id.

must_hit.point: Reconciliation posts adjustment journals for mismatches (never edit ledger history); cross-service payment+ledger+wallet uses saga/outbox with compensating refunds rather than pretending one distributed TX.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Classifies settlement mismatches into adjustment journals and names saga/outbox when services split.

probes: How do you get exactly-once business effect, and why isn’t a mutable wallet balance enough?

hints.1: Focus on retries, the ledger, and delayed PSP confirmation.
hints.2: Contrast key-before-PSP + double-entry with balance-only and sync-only designs.
hints.3: In-progress idempotency + PSP key; append-only balancing journal with same-TX wallet cache; pending + idempotent webhook on psp_event_id; recon via adjustment journals; saga/outbox across services.

phases.goal: Scale hot wallets, PSP outages, idempotency store, ledger growth, webhook storms, recon, and multi-region money writes safely.

must_hit.point: Hot merchant wallet row: optimistic versioning / row lock; for extreme credit fan-in, batch ledger flush or shard sub-accounts — trade fresher balance vs write amplification.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names wallet hotspot and versioning/batching/sharding options with the freshness tradeoff.

must_hit.point: PSP latency/outages: timeouts, circuit breaker per PSP, queue retries with backoff + jitter; never unbounded auto-retry without the same idempotency key; webhook storms → durable queue, concurrency limits, dedupe on event id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Protects against PSP failure and webhook floods without dropping idempotency.

must_hit.point: Ledger growth: partition by month, recent partitions for online queries, cold archive to object storage; recon streams settlement files keyed on psp_reference; multi-region usually single primary region for ledger + regional read replicas.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Partitions/archives ledger, keys recon joins, and avoids active-active money writes.

probes: What breaks first under a hot merchant or a PSP outage, and how do you keep money mutations safe?

hints.1: Think wallet row contention and dependency on the PSP.
hints.2: Add idempotent retries, webhook intake limits, and ledger partitioning.
hints.3: Version/lock or shard hot wallets; circuit breaker + backoff with same idempotency key; monthly ledger partitions; webhook dedupe; single primary region for ledger.

tradeoffs.topic: Persist idempotency (key → response) before calling PSP vs after
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Best practice: persist in-progress under the key, call PSP with a PSP-side idempotency key too, then finalize — same client key must never create two PSP charges; on replay compare params (Stripe rejects mismatched body).

tradeoffs.topic: Double-entry append-only ledger vs mutable balance only
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Balance-only is fast but loses audit trail and makes recon painful; double-entry append-only (≥2 journal lines summing to zero) is the interview answer, with cached wallets.balance updated in the same TX as ledger lines (or derived asynchronously with care).

tradeoffs.topic: Sync PSP call vs async webhook as source of truth
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sync is simpler UX; webhooks are source of truth for delayed/3DS methods — design for both: optimistic pending plus a durable webhook handler idempotent on psp_event_id; merchant webhooks need signature verify + idempotent delivery.

tradeoffs.topic: Single DB TX (payment + ledger + wallet) vs saga/outbox across services
tradeoffs.strong_answer: One DB is simple when colocated; cross-service needs saga/outbox with compensating refunds (Hello Interview multi-step / authorize→capture→ledger→webhook), plus transactional outbox so payment row and event publish are atomic.

tradeoffs.topic: Fresher merchant balance vs write amplification on hot wallet
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Optimistic versioning/row lock on the hot wallet row; for extreme credit fan-in, batch ledger flush or shard sub-accounts — call out fresher balance vs write amplification.

gotchas.trap: Timeout after charge — unclear whether money was taken; candidate creates a new Idempotency-Key on retry.
gotchas.correction: Ambiguous until you know; retry with the same idempotency key; reconcile with PSP list/get by key; never mint a new key on retry.

gotchas.trap: Claiming the network/PSP call is exactly-once.
gotchas.correction: You don’t get exactly-once on the wire; you guarantee exactly-once business effect via at-least-once delivery/retry plus an idempotent handler / idempotency key.

gotchas.trap: Wallet says one amount but bank/PSP says another — treated as a bug to silently overwrite.
gotchas.correction: Expected until settlement; reconciliation closes the gap; post adjustment journals and alert — never edit ledger history.

gotchas.trap: Storing raw card numbers in your DB/API.
gotchas.correction: Card data lives at the PSP via token / Elements hosted fields; keep PCI scope reduced (SAQ A-style if hosted fields only) — no PAN on your servers.

gotchas.trap: Refund after partial capture or double refund without a state machine.
gotchas.correction: Refund state machine + its own idempotency key; ledger posts reversing entries.

gotchas.trap: Outbox published but wallet/payment TX rolled back (or dual-write between payments row and queue).
gotchas.correction: Outbox row must be written in the same TX as the payment/ledger update; consumers stay idempotent because relay is still at-least-once.

gotchas.trap: Drawing microservices everywhere but no ledger.
gotchas.correction: Interviewers treat missing ledger/audit trail as a fail for payments — include immutable double-entry journal and reconciliation.
